text.content:
• Where from: each class has a d100 follower table (Strongholds by Class). It mixes units, retainers, artisans, ambassadors and the odd special ally, and isn't limited to that class's own retainers.
  • When you roll: when your stronghold is finished, at each upgrade, and each time you gain a Level while you hold it. That's roughly one roll per adventure.
    • The GM may roll in secret and pick, or simply award a follower for a great deed, stronghold or not.
  • Multiclass: a multiclass character picks which class table to roll on each time.

• What they are: retainers are henchmen (Handbook, Hiring) who came to you.
  • TAC's henchman rules apply:
    • They start at least one Level below you.
    • They gain Levels from party XP, never above yours.
    • They take half a share of treasure.
    • They have a Loyalty score and make Loyalty checks.
  • Starting Loyalty: your Charisma modifier + 2, because they sought you out.
  • Control: they obey. They don't take the lead or the spotlight.
  • Lieutenant:
    • One retainer, or a Captain artisan, can run the stronghold while you're away.
    • If your character dies, a lieutenant can become your new character.
  • Retainer frame: a retainer is a simplified character. A martial retainer has a weapon signature attack; a caster's is a cantrip.
StatRule
HealthOne health level per 2 Levels (minimum 2). No HP
When hitFortitude save, DC = the attack's average damage. Success: nothing. Failure: lose 1 health level per damage die
SpellsIt saves as normal. Success: lose half the spell's level (round down). Failure: lose the spell's level
DownAt 0 health levels it's dying (Handbook, Death & Dying)
Healing+1 health level per die of healing; all back on a full rest
ACBy the armour it wears
AttackLevel + 3. One signature attack a round; from Level 7, a second one at Disadvantage
SavesHalf Level + 3 on its two listed saves, half Level + 1 on the third
DC10 + half Level + 3
Skills+3 on its listed skills, +0 otherwise
Special actionsOne at Level 3 (once per encounter), one at 7 (once per day), one at 11 (once per day)
  • Fighting together:
    • The default: on your turn, if you hit an enemy (a damaging spell or one with a save counts), your retainer's signature attack hits too, against a target of your choice in its reach or range.
    • If you miss or don't attack: it rolls its own attack.
    • Either way: it moves and acts on your turn.
  • Kit: it starts with a starting character's kit for its class. Items you give it work normally, but it shouldn't outshine you.
  • The retainers themselves: each class's retainers (the Reaver, Curate, Tracker, Evoker, Cutpurse and more) are given in Strongholds by Class, in this frame.

• What they are: specialists who stay on after the build, or locals you helped.
  • Their shop:
    • Each one sets up a shop at 1st level for free. It goes up to 5th.
    • Upgrades cost 100, 150, 200 and 250 gp, and each takes a season. Paying more doesn't make it faster.
ArtisanShopEffect
AlchemistLaboratoryPotions you make cost and take 10% less per shop level. Harvests eyes and brains (below)
BlacksmithSmithyMagic arms and armour you make cost and take 10% less per level. Quenches slaying weapons (below)
ScribeScriptoriumScrolls you make cost and take 10% less per level, if the caster spends an hour with them. Also translation and diplomatic letters
CaptainBarracksOne unit per barracks level fights one step more experienced in a battle (you choose at the start; Warfare). Can be your lieutenant. Brings no troops
CarpenterWoodshopSiege engines cost 10% less per level, to build and keep. Stronghold upgrades take 10% less time per level
MasonQuarryFree repairs after a siege, worth 25 gp × level a week. Upgrades take 10% less time per level (with the carpenter, 50% at most)
FarmerMarket+10 gp a season
MinerMine+50 gp a season. One unit per mine level gets one step better gear (light to medium to heavy)
SageLibraryA week's research on one kind of creature: your next attack against it has Advantage, or ignores its Resistance, or its next save against you has Disadvantage. Uses equal library level per Extended Rest
SpyNetworkEnemy spies' checks against you are harder (DC +3 + network level). You may shift any follower roll by up to 3 + network level
TailorTailor's ShopTreat the d20 on one Charisma check as a 12. Uses equal shop level per Extended Rest

Monster harvests (Alchemist, Blacksmith, Scribe)

  • The rules: the Handbook's Making Magic Items rules still apply (who can make it, checks, Special Materials). The artisan only cuts the time and gold.
  • Timing: harvest within minutes of the kill, one try per body.
  • The checks: Hard Spellcraft to find the organ, then Healing or First Aid to take it: Moderate for a creature of Level 1 to 5, Hard for Level 6 to 12, Severe for Level 13+.
  • Range: each item works only against that exact kind of creature. A black dragon's eyes work on black dragons only.
OrganMakesArtisan
EyesPotion of invisibility to that creature (Uncommon)Alchemist
BrainPotion of control over that creature (Rare; as Dominate Monster, 1 hour)Alchemist
HeartScroll of protection from that creature (Uncommon)Scribe
BloodArrows of slaying for that creature: 1d6 arrows (Level 1 to 5), 1d4 (6 to 9), 2 (10 to 14), 1 (15+)Blacksmith
BloodA slaying weapon: a slashing weapon quenched in the blood deals +2d6 damage to that creature. It takes a nameBlacksmith

• What they are: each ambassador speaks for one people or polity (a particular orc clan, not all orcs).
  • What they give: you can raise or buy units of that people (Warfare) as if they were friendly.
  • What they aren't: a reward, not a spy. Any falling-out comes from play.

• What they are: powerful beings (a couatl, a young metallic dragon, a ki-rin) who approve of you.
  • What they do: they can't be ordered and won't always come, but they offer favours and quests.
  • Tables: each class table points to them, and Strongholds by Class gives the d20 tables by Outlook.

• Who can knight: a Knight of 21st level (Conversion to Knighthood) may knight a follower or any other NPC who has earned it. While a Knight holds Renown: Castle (20th), a follower who has served there a year may be knighted the same way.
  • The oath: the new knight is bound to the one who knighted them. They obey and keep the knightly code; if they break it, they lose the title and its benefits.
  • No class: a follower of 0 Level becomes a 1st-level Knight and a retainer (Retainers, above), built as the Banneret (Retainer Roster, Chapter 3).
  • A class already: they choose to stay in it or to take Knight as a second class, and serve as a retainer if they didn't already.
  • The accolade: a knighted follower has +1 AC and +1 damage on its weapon attacks, for good.
  • Pay: 4 gp a month per Level, from your scutage, as the Handbook's Renown: Castle says.

• Knight, Renown: Castle (Call to Arms, 20th): the castle is a keep, or a castle with a keep, held under these rules. Its followers and their scutage are as the Handbook says.
  • Knight, Battle Lord (19th): the Handbook keeps the part for ordinary fights. Leading units is in Warfare (Heroes in battle).
  • Knight, Conversion to Knighthood (21st): see Knighted followers, above.
  • Barbarian Warlord, Cleric Holy Campaign: these armies become units in Warfare.
  • Downtime: an Extended Rest is a downtime week. Learning, crafting and training run as the Handbook says, and a stronghold's artisans only cut the cost.
  • Divine Favour: used for petitions as it stands.
